column2: The first Tuesday of September, at the foot of the Columbus column by the port. Marc, a reserved locksmith with a deadpan humor, claims Columbus points not to America but to Mallorca, then admits "más o menos". Yuna is starting to catch his jokes. Light.

The library of Barcelona's maritime museum. A kind old librarian searches 1978 newspapers and finds that the Korean fishing boat "Dong-Hae 7" arrived from Las Palmas on 3 March 1978 with families aboard, and left on 12 November. Yuna meets the past tense for the first time ("llegó", "salió", "vivió", "hizo"); Marc explains it simply, including the stress difference between "llego" and "llegó". Tense, then moving.
calm, a little awed
curious, thinking, a real question

That evening in Montse's kitchen. Montse, now in her seventies, reads the two newspaper articles and remembers the boat's name. Slowly, without looking at Yuna, she says Yuna's mother was three and played in the patio with her cats. Yuna realizes her mother lived in this very house. Hushed and emotional, held back.
